| `block land` | Plain land, `--merge` with the selected-test merge gate, `--no-merge-gate`, active grants and `hooks.on_block_end`. A batch land's merge gate links `gates.merge_gate_links`, runs `gates.merge_gate_setup` and honours `--copy-links` like a single land (B589). A batch whose `--max` deadline runs out, in a block's rebase, changed gates or trial merge or in the merge gate, refuses the whole batch with no culprit and lands nothing (B662). A retry of a closed block (a land that failed after close) stays in Go when the run has active autopilot approvals, since the retry ends no block (B589). `land.require_ci: github` (opt in) checks GitHub CI for each block's own tip with `gh` before any hand-over, merge or write and refuses at step `ci` unless it is green or red only on known reds (`land.ci_red_list`, `CODE_FORGE_CI_RED_BLOCKS`) (B765). With it, a tip with no CI run is pushed in Go to a CI branch with a draft PR that replaces the stale one, land waits for CI up to `land.ci_wait` and refuses at the limit with the resume command, an SSH push that fails on auth is retried once over HTTPS with the gh credential helper (main's `--push` too), and the block's CI PRs are closed after the land (B796). With `native.daemon: false` land runs its review join in this process like `review-file --wait-block`, and a retry of a closed block needs no join at all, so the setting no longer stops land (B789). Since B797 land reads the base branch's reflog before it merges: since the last `code-forge land` entry (or the time of `<git common dir>/code-forge-guard/reviewed`), every entry must be a land, a `code-forge release`, or a fast-forward commit, merge or pull; anything else (a reset, an amend, a `branch -f`) refuses at step `main-reflog` and lists the entries, with `touch <reviewed>` to accept them after a check. The merge carries the guard token and the reflog action `code-forge land <ids>`. | The gates step (B450), no compatible join daemon while the daemon is on, the join, claim and close steps Go does not serve, and run state Go does not expect. A run file Go cannot read prints Node's read error in Go (B470). Read-only pre-checks finish before the first write. The B282 reason code names the step. `--help` and `-h` print the usage in Go (B451). |
